pattern.description: On the beat, the edit cuts from live-action footage of a player to first-person in-headset gameplay capture; the caption sentence ends with the live clip and a small 'Captured on PC.' disclaimer sits bottom-centre over the capture.
pattern.why_premium: Cutting on the music beat from the person to what they see sells the product promise in one frame, and the small, consistent disclaimer keeps the capture honest without competing with the gameplay.

build_hint.gsap: tl.set('.liveClip, .caption', {autoAlpha: 0}, beatTime).set('.captureClip, .disclaimer', {autoAlpha: 1}, beatTime); in-clip motion is source footage, so no tween; optionally add a 2-3% scale settle with fromTo('.captureClip', {scale: 1.03}, {scale: 1, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power2.out'}).
build_hint.remotion: Two back-to-back <Sequence> blocks cut on the beat frame; render the disclaimer as a static <AbsoluteFill> label inside the capture sequence. Optional settle: scale = interpolate(frame, [0, 12], [1.03, 1], {easing: Easing.out(Easing.quad), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}).

notes: Most motion after the cut is in-game first-person head movement, not a camera move added in the edit; camera.move says tilt_up for that reason. b02 ('Ace Haven') and b04 ('Court 2') are in-game signage moving with the scene, so they are covered by b01 rather than listed separately.
